title: President Trump furthers Michael Whatley support, attacks Cooper on crime, Helene - NewsBreak
text:
By Andy Weber ,
4 hours ago
GASTONIA, N.C. ( QUEEN CITY NEWS ) -- President Trump spent Wednesday night in Gastonia campaigning for Michael Whatley, the former RNC chair who is now running for a North Carolina U.S. Senate seat.
Trump said Whatley is the obvious choice.
“Nobody better in the whole country. I had my choice in the whole country. I chose Michael Whatley," he said.
Trump was quick to praise Whatley for his work during the 2024 presidential election.
“I said, when I win this thing, I'm going to take that guy from North Carolina and make him the head of the Republican Party, which is exactly what I did.”
Trump then took aim at Roy Cooper, the former governor and Whatley’s Democratic opponent in the closely watched Senate race.
“He’s a murderer protector... The man who made North Carolina the talk of our country. The whole country is talking about it for its violent crime. The radical left Democrat Roy Cooper," Trump accused.
Whatley, who also spoke Wednesday, pitched himself as the pro-public safety, pro-police candidate.
“They know that I am going to back the blue. I'm going to fight every single day to make sure we keep our kids and community safe," he said ahead of the rally.
Both Roy Cooper and North Carolina Democrats argued this week that Whatley and the president are focusing on the wrong issues.
“We see skyrocketing prices when we go to the grocery store, when we pass gas price signs like the one behind me, and when we go inside to buy a cup of coffee," State Senator Woodson Bradley (D-NC) said Wednesday morning in Gastonia.
In a statement issued ahead of the president’s remarks, a spokesperson for the Cooper campaign argued that claims about Roy Cooper’s public safety record are false, adding: “ Michael Whatley is getting desperate, and it’s shameful that he’s using heinous crimes to try to deceive North Carolinians. ”
With just under two months until the general election, polls still show Roy Cooper in the lead. An East Carolina poll gives Cooper a 7-point lead over Whatley. Early voting for the general election begins in mid-October.
